layers.title: The Root
layers.subtitle: What this Name means linguistically
layers.content:
The Name Allah (اللَّه)

The One True God

This Name appears among the 99 Names of Allah in the hadith of the Prophet: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' (Sahih Muslim)
layers.quran_ref: Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet said: Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise. — Sahih Muslim
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Meaning
layers.subtitle: The full understanding of this Name
layers.content: The name Allah indicates all of the perfect names and lofty attributes. Ibnul-Qayyim said: This name is not mentioned upon a small amount of something except that it causes it to increase. It is not mentioned in a state of fear except that it removes it, nor upon any misfortune except that it relieves it, nor in any state of anxiety except that it brings relief. None who is weak resorts to it except that it brings strength to him. None in a state of humiliation except that it brings honour. None in poverty except that he is enriched. It is the name through which distress is removed, through which the descent of blessings is sought, through which supplications are answered.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: In the Quran
layers.subtitle: Where Allah calls Himself by this Name
layers.content:
Allah calls Himself Allah in the Quran. The placement of each Name is not accidental — when Allah ends a verse with Allah, He is signalling that the meaning of that Name is the reason for what preceded the verse.

Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One

The scholars of tafseer note that knowing which Name closes which verse deepens understanding of the Quran itself. The Name is the key to the verse.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: The Scholar
layers.subtitle: Ibn Uthaymeen's explanation
layers.content:
Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen (rahimahullah), one of the foremost scholars of the 20th century, explained the Name Allah:

The name Allah indicates all of the perfect names and lofty attributes. Ibnul-Qayyim said: This name is not mentioned upon a small amount of something except that it causes it to increase. It is not mentioned in a state of fear except that it removes it, nor upon any misfortune except that it relieves it, nor in any state of anxiety except that it brings relief. None who is weak resorts to it except that it brings strength to him. None in a state of humiliation except that it brings honour. None in poverty except that he is enriched. It is the name through which distress is removed, through which the descent of blessings is sought, through which supplications are answered.

Ibn Uthaymeen taught that truly knowing the Names of Allah changes a person — not merely memorising them, but understanding their meaning and then living in light of them. He who knows Allah as Allah will relate to Allah differently, supplicate to Him differently, and trust in Him differently.
layers.source: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names of Allah

layers.title: Your Reflection
layers.subtitle: What this Name means for your life
layers.content:
The Name Allah is not only something to know about Allah — it is something to live in relation to.

The Prophet said: 'Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter paradise.' The word for enumerate — ahsaha — means to know, understand, act upon, and call upon Allah by each Name appropriately.

Reflect: When do you most need to call upon Allah as Allah? What situation in your life right now makes this particular Name the one you need most? The Names of Allah are not a list to memorise — they are doors to knock on in different moments of need.

The Quran says: 'And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them.' (7:180)

quiz.prompt: What is the primary meaning of the Name Allah?

options.text: The One True God
The All-Knowing
The Most Powerful
The Creator

quiz.citation: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Name Allah means the one true god. Understanding the precise meaning allows you to call upon Allah by this Name at the right moment.

quiz.prompt: How many Names does Allah have according to the hadith?

options.text: One hundred names
Ninety-nine — one hundred less one
Seventy-two names
The Names are unlimited in number

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim — Verily to Allah belongs ninety-nine names, one hundred less one
quiz.scholar_reflection: The scholars note that Allah has more Names than ninety-nine — these are the specific Names He has revealed to us. The ninety-nine are a door; what lies beyond is immeasurable.

quiz.prompt: In which Quranic context does the Name Allah appear?

options.text: Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One
Quran 1:1 — In the name of Allah, Ar-Rahman, Ar-Raheem
Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, Al-Ahad
Quran 2:255 — The Throne Verse

quiz.citation: Quran 112:1 — Say: He is Allah, the One
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Quran places each Divine Name in a specific context. Allah is telling you, through the Name He chose, why He did what He did. The Name is the key to the verse.

quiz.prompt: What does 'enumerating' (ahsaha) the Names of Allah mean?

options.text: Memorising all 99 in Arabic
Knowing, understanding, acting upon, and calling upon Allah by each Name
Counting them on prayer beads daily
Writing them in calligraphy

quiz.citation: Ibn Uthaymeen, Commentary on the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: Memorisation is the beginning. The Names become alive when you call upon Al-Mujeeb when you need response, Al-Ghafoor when you need forgiveness, Al-Lateef when you need subtle help.

quiz.prompt: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen passed away in which year?
quiz.citation: Publisher's note — Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen commentary
quiz.scholar_reflection: Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen spent more than 50 years teaching and guiding people to worship Allah. He authored more than 40 books and is considered one of the most pre-eminent scholars of the 20th century.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Allah — the one true god. When in your life have you most needed Him to be this for you?
quiz.slider_label: How often do you call upon Allah by this specific Name?

options.text: In a moment of fear or danger
When I needed something no one else could provide
When I felt ashamed or broken
I have not thought about needing this quality specifically

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Names of Allah become real to us in the moments we need them most. Each Name is a door — Allah placed exactly this Name in your path at exactly this moment.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet said whoever enumerates the Names enters paradise. What is the relationship between knowing Allah's Names and paradise?
quiz.slider_label: How connected is your knowledge of Allah to your actions?

options.text: Knowing Who Allah truly is makes you unable to live as if He does not exist
The Names change how you relate to Allah in worship
Understanding the Names removes the distance between you and Him
All of the above — true knowledge of Allah transforms everything

quiz.citation: Sahih Muslim — the hadith of the 99 Names
quiz.scholar_reflection: You do not enter paradise merely by reciting a list. You enter because true knowledge of Allah reshapes who you are — your love, your fear, your trust, your worship.

quiz.prompt: Allah is Allah. How does knowing this specific quality of Allah change how you make du'a?
quiz.slider_label: How specifically do you call upon Allah in your du'a?

options.text: I call upon Him by this Name when I need what it describes
I have not thought about matching the Name to the need
It makes me more confident that my du'a is heard
It makes me more specific about what I am asking for

quiz.citation: Reflection on calling upon Allah as Allah
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Quran says: And to Allah belong the best Names, so call upon Him by them. Calling upon Al-Ghafoor for forgiveness is not the same as calling upon Al-Qadir for strength. Match the Name to the need.

quiz.prompt: One fruit of knowing Allah's Names is muhabbah — love of Allah. What makes it difficult to love someone you cannot see?
quiz.slider_label: How much of your relationship with Allah is based on knowing Who He is?

options.text: Love requires knowing — and knowing Allah requires learning His Names
We love what benefits us — and He is the source of all benefit
We love beauty — and He is Al-Jameel, The Beautiful
Love of Allah comes through experiencing His mercy in your own life

quiz.citation: Reflection on muhabbah — love of Allah
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn al-Qayyim said the heart is created with a nature to love — and it will love something. The Names of Allah, when known, make Him the most worthy object of that love.

quiz.prompt: If you spent one week consciously remembering that Allah is Allah — what would change in your daily life?
quiz.slider_label: How present is Allah in your daily awareness?

options.text: My anxiety would decrease — I would trust more
My du'a would become more specific and sincere
I would behave differently knowing He is aware
I would feel less alone in whatever I am facing

quiz.citation: Practical reflection on the Name Allah
quiz.scholar_reflection: The purpose of knowing the Names is taqwa — constant awareness of Allah. Not fear alone, but awareness. When you are aware of Al-Qareeb, you are never truly alone.
